title: Decimal Computation: Line Up, Then Operate
preview: Anchor on simple decimal addition, then build through all four operations — each with its own decimal-point rule. Pairs naturally with the Fluency drills for individual practice.

body.goal: Students articulate the place-value rules for each of the four operations on multi-digit decimals — line up the decimal for add/subtract, count places for multiply, shift for divide.
body.launch: Open with the prerequisite warm-up so they're locked in on place value. Then run the slice. Don't pre-teach the rules — let the variation reveal them. After the slice, send them to the Fluency Practice tool for individual reps.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up: what does each digit mean?

prerequisiteSteps.problem: What digit is in the tenths place of 3.06?

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Decimal moves one place left when you multiply by 10.
Decimal moves one place right when you divide by 10.

steps.teacherNote: Anchor — same number of decimal places, no carrying.
Vary one thing: one operand has an extra decimal place. Push 'line up the decimal point, not the right edge.'
Carrying across the decimal point. Result is 6.10 = 6.1.
Tenths only, but the sum carries past the ones place.
Switch to subtraction — same alignment rule still works.
Uneven places. Pad 5.0 with a hidden trailing 0.
Whole number minus decimal. Treat 10 as 10.0 to align.
Subtraction with borrowing through the decimal.
Switch to multiplication. Push: 'multiply ignoring the decimals (4 × 3 = 12), then count TOTAL decimal places in the factors and shift.'
Switch to division. Keep the decimal aligned with the dividend.
Decimal divisor — shift both decimals one place right (×10/×10 = ×1) to get 4.8 ÷ 4 = 1.2.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Chain of operations — alignment rule for each step.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'In one sentence, what's the rule for adding or subtracting decimals?' Push for 'line up the decimal point.' Then: 'What's the rule for multiplying decimals?' Push for 'multiply ignoring the decimals, then count total decimal places.' Then point them at the Fluency Practice button on this section — same skill, individual reps.
